meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Company regime regulated by the Samoa International Financial Authority, Apia)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (unitary national system; customary law confined to land and matai title matters)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 10–14 (incorporation), s. 24 (registered office and registered agent); International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018 (mandatory register of beneficial owners); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2019; Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Regulations; Samoa International Financial Authority Act 2013; SIFA AML/CFT Rulebook and Customer Due Diligence Directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank of the investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The proposed International Company (all subscribers), executed before a notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU and UK HMT consolidated sanctions lists, Interpol notices, and Samoa's domestic AML/CFT watchlists; Politically Exposed Persons and their family members or close associates trigger enhanced due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2019 and SIFA directives.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) — International Companies Registry, Apia (filing via SIFA-licensed corporate service providers; no fully automated public e-portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in Latin-script English or Romanized Samoan and must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Public Limited Company', or an accepted abbreviation (Ltd., Corp., Inc., PLC). A Chinese-language secondary trade name (中文商號) may be reserved simultaneously, but a certified Roman-script transliteration and English translation must accompany the incorporation application. The articles may be drafted entirely in Chinese provided a certified English translation is filed with the Registrar.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chinese equivalents (银行, 信托, 保险, 金融, 政府, 皇家) — statutorily restricted tokens requiring prior ministerial or regulatory approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The proposed name must be pre-cleared by the Registrar of International Companies before incorporation. Upon rejection, the applicant may either conduct a fresh name search with a revised name or lodge a written administrative appeal to the Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of distinctiveness and non-confusion. SIFA must issue a written determination within 15 working days; an aggrieved applicant may then seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the statutory registered office. The International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa (street address in Apia, no P.O. Box acceptable), serviced by a SIFA-licensed registered agent and corporate service provider. Remote back-office administrative functions are permissible, but the registered agent must maintain full physical premises, personnel, and statutory records in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this standard-risk commercial profile; approximate 10-15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registrar or the Financial Intelligence Unit during the first 12 months, increasing materially upon adverse media coverage, sanctions alerts, or suspicious transaction report triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss.5–13 (Incorporation and Registration), s.9 (name restrictions), s.12 (Certificate of Incorporation), s.103 (registered agent), s.134 (exemption for offshore business); subsidiary forms under the International Companies (Amendment) Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Government of Samoa, Apia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration of the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association using Form 1 (Notice of Registration of an International Company) under the International Companies Act 1987
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The company must issue at least one share to the initial subscriber; share capital may be expressed in any currency, paid-up capital may be nominal, and no escrow account or capitalized reserves are required by the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first board meeting of the Company: 1. That one ordinary share of no par value be allotted at USD 1.00 to the initial subscriber, and the subscriber be entered in the register of members. 2. That the registered office be fixed at the registered agent's office in Apia, Samoa, and the licensed agent's services be retained under the International Companies Act 1987. 3. That [Director A] and [Director B] be appointed directors, and [Officer] be appointed secretary. 4. That any one director, acting with the secretary, may execute banking and corporate documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL – International Companies Registry, Apia (filings submitted through a licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance application to the Registrar of International Companies. The proposed name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or equivalent, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Samoan company or international company. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days. Subscriber identification is obtained by the registered agent for AML/KYC purposes.
required_dossiers: Subscriber identification documents (notarized passport copy or certificate of incumbency)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised name immediately or request an administrative review by the Registrar; name search fees are partly credited toward the final incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Signing and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoan registered agent and notary public in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English. The documents must state the company name, registered office in Samoa, limited liability clause, authorized share structure, and corporate objects. The subscriber executes the documents before a notary public, and the registered agent certifies compliance with the International Companies Act 1987. Consents of directors and secretary are obtained in prescribed statutory form.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or execution is defective, the notary issues a corrective certification and replacement execution pages are signed; no additional state fee is charged within the same filing package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Package to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form 1, consents of directors and secretary, and registered office consent. Submission is made electronically through the MCIL companies portal or physically at the Companies Office in Apia. The Registrar stamps the application and issues an acknowledgment within one business day.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Notice of Registration of an International Company
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office consent and address certificate
Director and secretary consents and particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query under s.13, cure the stated deficiency within 14 days by filing an amended Form 1 and a letter of explanation; the incorporation is completed once all queries are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Statutory Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL cashier / Samoa Treasury payment gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official state filing fee of USD 150 (or the equivalent in Samoa Tala WST) plus any applicable stamp duty. Upload the payment receipt to the incorporation record. Upon confirmation of payment and compliance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under s.12 of the International Companies Act 1987, which is conclusive evidence of corporate existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a payment discrepancy is identified, a Treasury reconciliation memo is filed and the exact fee is re-confirmed; the Certificate of Incorporation is released upon reconciliation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent under the International Companies Act 1987, s.103
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the licensed registered agent has established the registered office at a physical street address in Apia. The agent files notice of appointment and the registered office address details with the Registrar for inclusion in the public register. The company pays the first-year registered agent fee as invoiced.
required_dossiers: First-year annual registered agent fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or is deregistered, the directors must appoint another licensed agent within 30 days and file a change of registered office notice; non-compliance may lead to striking off the register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Establishment of Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and corporate secretary (meeting may be conducted by unanimous written resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt a unanimous written resolution passing the pro-forma first board resolution. Issue the share certificate to the initial subscriber, open statutory registers of members, directors and secretary, approve the corporate seal, and maintain the minutes and registers at the registered office in Apia. The meeting may be held outside Samoa; no quorum filing is required for the first board meeting.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution as approved
Register of members, directors and secretary
Minutes of first board meeting or written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omission or defect in the corporate records is cured by a subsequent unanimous written resolution ratified by all directors; no public filing consequence arises for internal record rectification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable to a Samoa International Company conducting fully offshore contract manufacturing. Contingent authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Business Licence Section and the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) if any physical manufacturing facility is later established in Samoa.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – the offshore business is exempt from local business licensing under s.134 of the International Companies Act 1987; a contingent Business Licence under the Samoa Business Licence Act 2013 (Manufacturing/Wholesale category) would apply only to domestic Samoan activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA required for incorporation or offshore contract manufacturing abroad; a Preliminary EIA (Registration tier) would be triggered only for a local factory, assembly unit or warehouse established in Samoa.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Offshore operations are subject to the jurisdiction of the manufacturing country. If a Samoa local site is created, compliance would be required with the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004, Waste Management Act 2009, and World Bank/IFC EHS Guidelines for plastic injection molding: VOC workplace limits of 3 mg/m3, noise not exceeding 75 dBA at plant boundary, wastewater pH 6–9, and segregated recovery of scrap plastic and packaging waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable offshore. Contingently, any local office or warehouse would require a fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA), structural load compliance under the Samoa Building Code, and a workplace occupational safety inspection clearance from the Ministry of Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue of Samoa (MOR), Government of Samoa; official taxpayer portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws (STAR e-Services)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity is required to obtain a Samoa TIN only if it carries on a taxable activity in Samoa, derives Samoan-source income, or is required to withhold Samoan tax; a Samoa International Company (IC) is formed by lodging the registration application through a licensed international registered agent with the Registrar of International Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour / Samoa International Finance Authority), and the Certificate of Incorporation serves as the primary statutory identifier. Where a TIN is needed (bank account opening, VAGST registration, employer registration), the IC files the MOR Application Form for Taxpayer Identification Number with the Ministry of Revenue, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, Constitution, registered agent certificate, and Samoan office or agent address; the MOR issues the TIN within 10 business days. For the standard offshore IC in Tax_Exempt_Zone status conducting no Samoan taxable activity and deriving no Samoan-source income, no TIN, VAGST registration, or income tax filing is required; the only statutory payment obligation is the annual international company government license fee remitted through the registered agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box regime and has not enacted domestic OECD hybrid-mismatch rules. Available elections: (1) conversion of an IC to an ordinary domestic company under the Companies Act 2006, electing into the standard Samoa income tax and VAGST regimes; (2) continuance or redomiciliation of a foreign company as a Samoa IC under the International Companies Act 1987, electing into the offshore tax-exempt regime; (3) application to the MOR for a certificate of tax residence or non-residence for CRS, FATCA, and treaty relief purposes; (4) adoption of provisions in the IC's Constitution confining its business to offshore activities in order to preserve the statutory tax exemption. No election is available to treat the IC as a pass-through entity for Samoan income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2007 (as amended), supplemented by customs and excise duties under the Customs Act 1977 and Excise Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 50,000 per annum: a person carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa whose taxable supplies exceed or are likely to exceed SAT 50,000 in any consecutive 12-month period must register for VAGST; non-residents register only if they make taxable supplies connected with Samoa, so the offshore IC selling mecha model kits exclusively to foreign buyers sits below the threshold and outside the Samoan registration nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (API), or digital stamping mandate exists in Samoa. A VAGST-registered business must issue a valid tax invoice within 7 days of supply, containing the prescribed particulars (supplier name and TIN, invoice number and date, description of goods, consideration, and VAGST separately stated). The MOR's STAR system supports electronic return filing and voluntary e-invoicing, but compliance is enforced through post-return audit rather than pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods are zero-rated under the GST Act when sold under a taxable supply in Samoa and physically exported within the statutory export window (generally 30 days, subject to extension for containerized shipments), provided the supplier retains full documentary proof of export. Services are zero-rated when performed outside Samoa, enjoyed wholly outside Samoa, or supplied to a recipient who is outside Samoa at the time of supply; the IC's offshore design, molding, assembly, and sale of ISIC 3240 action-figure mecha model kits to non-resident buyers is therefore outside Samoan VAGST and, where a Samoan-registered entity invoices the export, qualifies for the 0% rate with recovery of any attributable input credits. Refund claims are payable by the MOR within 30 days of a complete submission.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Service Export Declaration (electronic CUS-EXP entry, HS 9503.00 attribution for toys and action figures)
Bill of Lading, House Bill of Lading, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement advice evidencing receipt of foreign customer funds
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying SKUs, quantities, unit prices, and ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930 description
VAGST zero-rated tax invoice issued to the non-resident buyer
Manufacturer's or supplier's certificate of origin (required for PTA/EPA claims or buyer confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The MOR may reverse a zero-rating claim, claw back refunds, and re-assess VAGST at 15% plus statutory interest where export documentation is deficient, invoices are false, or goods are diverted into the Samoan domestic market. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2012 escalate from 20% of the shortfall for failure to take reasonable care, to 40% for recklessness, 80% for intentional disregard, and up to 150% for deliberate evasion or concealment, with monthly late-payment penalties on top up to the statutory cap. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent zero-rating, forged bills of lading, or fabricated Inward Remittance Certificates may result in significant monetary fines and/or imprisonment of up to 5 years; for an International Company, the Registrar of International Companies may additionally strike the company off, and the offshore tax-exempt status can be revoked retroactively, rendering the entity assessable on its Samoan-source export margin.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia, Samoa – statutory monetary authority and exchange-control administrator under the Exchange Control Act and the International Companies Act 1987.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is not freely convertible spot currency; CBS operates an exchange-control regime that distinguishes current-account transactions, which are largely delegated to licensed authorized dealers (commercial banks), from capital-account transactions, which require CBS approval or notification. For an International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 and conducting all business outside Samoa with non-resident counterparties, the exchange-control licensing burden is generally disapplied: the IC may hold and remit foreign currency through an offshore-express account without CBS conversion clearance. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is lawful and normally unencumbered where the IC has no Samoan-resident creditor, no Samoan-source business income, and no WST-denominated liabilities. Practical hurdles arise when funds are converted into WST, when a Samoan resident is a counterparty, when the IC receives funds from a Samoan bank account, or when there is insufficient documentary evidence of the underlying non-Samoan trade; in such cases CBS may treat the remittance as resident profit repatriation and require board resolutions, audited financial statements, tax clearance, beneficial-ownership attestation, and balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBS exchange-control framework, a Samoa-resident exporter must collect export proceeds within 90 days from the date of export and must surrender 100% of the declared foreign-currency export proceeds to a licensed authorized dealer, except where a specific retention approval or export-account facility has been granted by CBS. A Samoa International Company that manufactures or purchases action-figure and mecha-model kits entirely through offshore contract manufacturers, never imports the goods into Samoa customs territory, and settles suppliers and customers through offshore USD accounts is treated as outside the physical export surrender obligation. However, if any leg of the transaction touches a Samoan bank account, the collecting bank will apply the 90-day repatriation rule, require underlying invoices and customs or shipping evidence, and may compel conversion into WST unless the CBS retention exemption is obtained in advance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Contribution USD Account / Operational Foreign-Currency Account
Operational WST Settlement Account / Trade Disbursement Account
Corporate USD Trust and Third-Party Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a treasury depository; Medium as a peripheral receivable or e-commerce settlement side-rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Airwallex are not licensed banks or authorized dealers by CBS, and Samoa does not recognize non-resident EMI client accounts as protected deposits. A Samoa International Company may use an EMI for collecting PayPal and small retail customer receipts, but balances must be swept promptly to a tier-1 Samoan licensed bank. Legal constraints include: exchange-control restrictions on routing funds through non-authorized financial institutions, AML/CFT travel-rule compliance, inability to obtain CBS confirmation for the EMI as a settlement rail for letters of credit, and heightened source-of-funds questions when large amounts are held offshore in an unregulated wallet. The EMI should never be used for capital injection, supplier letters of credit, or statutory liquidity evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A strict physical-presence rule is not absolute, but in practice at least one natural-person director, the ultimate beneficial owner, or a designated authorized signatory must undergo a face-to-face interview with the compliance officer of the Samoan bank. Remote video-KYC is accepted by some tier-1 banks for a Low-Risk Standard manufacturing entity where: (a) the IC is introduced by a licensed Samoa registered agent; (b) original notarized corporate documents, incumbency certificates, and source-of-funds files are couriered; and (c) the beneficial owner holds a passport from an FATF-compliant jurisdiction. For USD offshore-express accounts, most banks require a physical onboarding visit by the beneficial owner or a board-authorized signatory before the account is activated; subsequent directors may open by remote attestation through the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt International Company flagged as a tax-haven conduit with no local commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing; registered office and registered agent certificate; board resolution confirming all operations are conducted outside Samoa; audited or reviewed financial statements reflecting the Hong Kong/China manufacturing supply chain; customer and supplier contracts; invoices and shipping documents; tax-residence certificate of the ultimate beneficial owner; and a written business plan evidencing the action-figure and mecha-model kit manufacturing value chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layered or nominee shareholding structure causing inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate ownership chart to natural persons; copies of passports and proof of residential address for all qualifying beneficial owners; trust deed or declaration of trust if held through a Samoa trust; register of members and register of beneficial owners prepared under the International Companies Act; certified source-of-funds bank statements for at least 24 months; and professional reference letters from a regulated attorney, accountant, or international corporate services provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered agent or nominee director arrangement without clear authority or economic ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed registered agent certificate; nominee director declaration disclaiming beneficial interest; executed power of attorney and board minutes delegating banking authority; strategic management records showing the non-resident directors control commercial decisions; and a CBS-compliant register detailing the relationship between the nominee, the IC, and the ultimate shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PayPal and small-retail receivables creating perceived AML exposure or high chargeback risk in toy/anime merchandise sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Distributor and licensee agreements; pro-forma invoices; shipping and customs records; product liability or product-safety insurance; PayPal business-account verification and 12-month settlement history; OFAC/sanctions screening reports for all counterparties; and an internal treasury policy restricting PayPal balances and requiring daily sweeping to the authorized bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital should be routed by the non-resident shareholder from its own bank account at a recognized international bank directly to the IC's USD account at a tier-1 Samoan licensed bank through SWIFT MT103. The wire must reference the Samoa IC registration number, the shareholder name, and the appropriate balance-of-payments purpose code for equity capital inward investment, typically mapped by the receiving bank as 'Direct Investment – Equity' or an equivalent CBS BOP capital-import code. Before remittance, the IC must adopt a board resolution approving the share subscription, issue share allotment letters, update the register of members, and prepare a source-of-funds dossier for the shareholder. The receiving bank will report any significant cash or wire transaction at or above the CBS threshold to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and may request audited financials or a capital statement. If the funds are to be converted into WST, CBS exchange-control approval may be required; if the shareholder is a Samoan resident, the transaction is treated as a resident capital movement and will require additional CBS consent. For a standard non-resident capital injection retained in USD, no CBS capital-import approval is generally required and the funds can be immediately used for offshore trade payments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments for the high-precision steel injection molding and snap-fit plastic kit supply chain should use SWIFT MT103 for direct invoice settlements from the IC's USD account at the Samoan authorized dealer to the Chinese or Hong Kong supplier's USD account; the payment must reference the supplier invoice, purchase order, and ISIC 3240 goods description. For high-value mold tooling and first-article production molds, an irrevocable, confirmed at-sight Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Samoan bank and advised through the supplier's bank is recommended to mitigate performance and delivery risk. For recurring raw-material purchases, documentary collections with documents against payment or documents against acceptance can be used. PayPal is acceptable only as an inbound retail-receivable rail and must not be used for outbound supplier disbursements because it is not a true clearing system, carries chargeback risk, and lacks the documentary evidence required by CBS for trade payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/WST forward contracts with a CBS-licensed authorized dealer, limited to the amount of documented Samoan operating costs or WST liabilities and with a maturity not exceeding 12 months.

USD/WST cross-currency swaps with a licensed Samoan commercial bank for matching long-term foreign-currency share capital against a WST-denominated local expense base arising from future Samoan operations.
USD/WST foreign-exchange swaps for managing timing differences between USD capital injections and WST payroll or utility obligations.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD entered into with an OECD-regulated bank outside Samoa, permissible only as a commercial hedge of projected Samoan operating cash flows where no actual WST delivery is intended and the underlying exposure is fully documented.

Interest-rate and currency swaps linked to a project finance or trade-finance facility, provided the hedge is board-approved, non-speculative, and supported by an underlying invoice, purchase order, or treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form IC-AR) of an International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 45 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 50 per month or part month; failure to file for 6 consecutive months may lead to administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Licence Fee (Annual Franchise Fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Ministry of Finance / Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on or before each anniversary of incorporation; grace period of 2 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional penalty of 10% of the unpaid fee; if unpaid for 3 months after due date, the International Company may be struck off the Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation of Registered Office, Registered Agent, Directors, Members and Ultimate Beneficial Owner Information (part of Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted concurrently with the Annual Return on the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misstatement or omission may be treated as a false declaration; subject to criminal penalty and possible strike-off for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to an International Company under the Samoa International Companies Act 2009, unless the articles, shareholders, or the Registrar require an audit; audits are typically voluntary for tax-exempt non-resident owned entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as permitted under the International Companies Act 2009; alternatively, the company may maintain accounts prepared on a basis acceptable to the registered agent showing true and fair financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each International Company must maintain at its registered office a confidential Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges, and a Minute Book. The Annual Return must confirm the identity of members holding shares, directors, registered agent, and any changes in shareholding or ultimate beneficial ownership during the year; no public beneficial ownership filing is required, but the registered agent must retain a current beneficial ownership statement on file and submit it to the Registrar upon request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Ownership (confidential, maintained by registered agent or company)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,200 annual registered agent and registered office service fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (audit not required); if voluntarily appointed, typical certified audit fee ranges from USD 2,000 - USD 5,000 for a small trading entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (standard domestic corporate rate); 0% effective for an International Company (IC) by statutory exemption under s.204 of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are exempt from income tax, payroll tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and all other Samoan revenue laws; the sole annual cost is the fixed government license fee payable to the SAMOA International Finance Authority (SIFA); no tax is imposed on foreign-sourced income, and no dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees paid to non-residents are subject to Samoan withholding tax by reason of the IC exemption

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return and License Fee Renewal Form (SIFA IC-AR) — submitted by the licensed registered agent through the SIFA online service portal; no corporate income tax return is required to be filed with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue while the IC remains tax-exempt
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the anniversary of the date of registration (each year), followed by a 60-day administrative grace period; the annual license fee is payable for each year of continuation; failure to pay within the grace period triggers late penalty accrual and eventual strike-off

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact registered name of the International Company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Certificate of Incorporation and the SIFA register; no trade names permitted without separate registration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registration number (Company No.) issued by the Registrar of International Companies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the unique IC number; used for fee reconciliation and validation of good standing
The registered office must be a physical address within Samoa, maintained by the licensed agent; P.O. box alone is insufficient

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and license number of the registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must hold a valid license under the International Companies Act; the non-resident beneficial owner cannot act as the registered agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationality, and occupation of all directors
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permissible; nominee directors must be disclosed to the registered agent for AML/CFT records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, shareholdings, and classes of shares of all shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; non-resident shareholders, including corporate trustees, must be identified with underlying beneficial owner details per the AML/CFT Act 2018

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that no business was carried on within Samoa during the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC must not derive Samoan-source revenue; any domestic business activity voids the tax exemption and exposes the entity to 27% corporate tax, withholding, and penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC holds no real property or fixed assets in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Samoan real property would constitute domestic investment and trigger a separate licensing or taxation consequence; keeping the declaration negative is critical to preserving exempt status

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual license fee payment authorization and electronic signature of the registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is typically made by wire from the attorney trust account; the beneficial owner must remit funds to the agent in advance of the anniversary date

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late renewal after the 60-day grace period attracts a penalty of 50% of the applicable annual license fee; continued non-payment for more than 90 days leads to administrative strike-off from the SIFA register, automatic cessation of legal existence, forfeiture of assets to the Crown unless restored, and disqualification complexities for subsequent applications

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Company Income Tax Return (Form CIR-1) — filed electronically through the Samoa Ministry of Revenue e-Filing portal (applicable only if the IC inadvertently becomes a resident taxpayer by breaching the exemption conditions)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The income year is the calendar year unless otherwise approved; the return is due six months after the end of the income year (i.e., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end), with a discretionary extension of up to two months available on prior written application

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from Samoa sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company, only Samoan-source income is assessable; a foreign-incorporated entity with a Samoan permanent establishment must allocate income accordingly
The IC is tax-exempt and not assessable on foreign income; if the IC is reclassified as resident, worldwide income becomes taxable at 27%

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable deductions (excluding capital expenditure and non-deductible entertainment)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are permitted only where incurred in gaining assessable income and supported by contemporaneous records; related-party payments must satisfy the arm's length standard
Derived as Box 1a plus Box 1b less Box 2; no deduction is allowed for distributions to shareholders
Self-assessment; the rate applies to the entire taxable income without progressive bands for companies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding credits and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are available only where a double taxation agreement applies and a valid Tax Residence Certificate has been obtained; uncredited excess is not refundable
Payment is due on or before the filing deadline; failure triggers late payment interest and recovery measures including departure prohibition orders

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the assessed tax (minimum 20 penalty units) plus late payment interest of 2% per month compounded on the outstanding amount; deliberate non-filing or false declarations constitute tax evasion punishable by a further penalty of up to 150% of the short-paid tax and imprisonment up to 2 years

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (non-resident dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2015); reduced to 0% for an International Company's distributions to non-resident shareholders by virtue of the s.204 exemption, provided the IC has not breached its exempt-status conditions
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa maintains a limited double taxation agreement network; the principal comprehensive DTA in force is with New Zealand. To invoke treaty relief, a non-resident shareholder/beneficial owner must: (i) request a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its own residence-country tax authority; (ii) submit the TRC, a treaty relief declaration, and self-declaration of beneficial ownership to the Samoan payer or to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue; (iii) obtain confirmation of the reduced withholding rate before remittance; (iv) where the full 15% statutory rate has been withheld, file a claim for refund within the limitation period using the prescribed treaty claim form. The Samoa–NZ DTA maintains the 15% ceiling on dividends, 15% on interest, and 15% on royalties; no other bilateral treaty in force offers a lower rate for Samoan-source payments to Chinese or other non-resident recipients
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under the Income Tax Act 2015: interest 15%, royalties 15%, and management/technical fees 15% when paid to a non-resident; an International Company is exempt from withholding on such outbound payments to non-residents unless the payment is attributable to a Samoan business or the exemption is forfeited; under the Samoa–NZ DTA the treaty rate remains 15% for interest and royalties, and no domestic reduction exists for payments to related parties absent a TRC

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable in Samoa — no Local File / Master File regime has been enacted; the Income Tax Act 2015 contains a general arm's length rule for cross-border related-party transactions of taxable persons; because a fully exempt International Company pays no Samoan income tax, no mandatory TP documentation threshold applies in WST, but contemporaneous pricing evidence is prudent for any transactions with Samoan counterparties or if exemption status is challenged
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019, adopted in response to EU Code of Conduct Group requirements, impose a substance test on ICs that carry on specified 'relevant activities' (banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, distribution and service centre, intellectual property holding, and holding company). High-precision injection molding of action figure and mecha model kits (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930) is not a specified relevant activity, so no local substance requirement in Samoa arises from manufacturing alone. Nevertheless, the IC must not be a mere shell: it must maintain a registered office and licensed agent in Samoa, keep proper books and records, be administered at a board level outside Samoa, and conduct no domestic Samoan business. If a manufacturing IC earns passive income or continues to hold royalty/licensing assets derived from the toy designs without operational substance in its jurisdiction of control, Samoan or foreign tax authorities may disregard the exemption or reclassify the entity as effectively managed in a higher-tax jurisdiction, triggering 27% taxation or aggressive anti-avoidance reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company as a conduit for Samoan-source retail sales, importation, warehousing, payroll, or leasing activities while continuing to claim the s.204 tax exemption; deliberately understating the degree of Samoan activity in the annual return; or failing to notify SIFA and the Ministry of Revenue that the company has become a tax resident through central management and control in Samoa
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IC exemption is void ab initio for the year of the breach; the company is assessed on 27% corporate income tax on all income attributable to Samoan operations, plus non-resident withholding tax liabilities on any outbound payments; the Tax Administration Act 2015 imposes a civil penalty of up to 150% of the short-paid tax and a fine not exceeding 100 penalty units, and knowingly making a false declaration constitutes an offence punishable by imprisonment not exceeding 2 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally and jointly liable for the company's unpaid tax where they signed false declarations or directed the breach; the Ministry of Revenue may issue a departure prohibition order (travel ban) preventing any director or principal officer from leaving Samoa until the assessment, penalties, and interest are settled; judges may also award civil restitution against directors in proceedings brought by liquidators or creditors of the company

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as a bare title-holder of the toy manufacturing business with no real control, employees, premises, or transaction logic in its claimed jurisdiction of management; failing to file the annual return or to record board minutes and transfer pricing rationale; claiming tax residency in Samoa or abroad without any operational reality (e.g., a Chinese family trust holding the IC with no local substance in Samoa and no manufacturing presence anywhere)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019, a relevant IC that fails the economic substance test may be penalized up to WS$25,000, and a second-year failure may lead to deregistration by the Registrar; the entity may be treated as a sham for tax purposes, resulting in the imposition of 27% tax and penalties, and may be placed on international defensive-measure lists (EU Annex) that blacklist the structure for EU counterparties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit the company to operate with no economic substance or who sign certificates of good standing knowing the company is a façade are exposed to personal civil liability for abuse of process and fraudulent preference; the Registrar may disqualify directors for up to five years; regulators in the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction (e.g., China) may impose personal criminal or administrative penalties for cross-border tax evasion; travel bans may be imposed by Samoa for unpaid regulatory fines

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Integrity Breaches
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving customer payments via PayPal or SWIFT wires for the sale of action figure and mecha model kits while failing to maintain an effective AML/CFT framework; the IC being used as a pass-through for undisclosed third-party proceeds, nominee shareholding without identification of the beneficial owner, or transactions with sanctioned distributors or customers in restricted markets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoa AML/CFT Act 2018, a body corporate that fails to comply with customer due diligence, record-keeping, or suspicious transaction reporting obligations is liable to a fine not exceeding WS$1,000,000; the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) may impose a freezing order on the IC's bank accounts; wilful money laundering carries a custodial sentence of up to 10 years and confiscation of the proceeds of crime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and the registered agent are personally liable where the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect; sanctions include personal fines up to WS$250,000, imprisonment up to 5 years, forfeiture of commissions, and disqualification from serving as a director of any Samoa company; the director may also be subject to a restraint order over personal assets and a travel ban pending investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend Stripping and Improper Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring distributions or paying royalties, management fees, or interest to a foreign parent or trust while the IC is technically taxable (e.g., because foreign business is managed in Samoa); or structuring the pay-outs with no regard to the 15% statutory withholding tax, or failing to obtain a TRC before remitting treaty-protected payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Ministry of Revenue may treat the entire distribution as a constructive dividend, impose 15% non-resident withholding tax on the gross amount, add a penalty of up to 150% for non-declaration, and charge interest at 2% per month; additionally, thin capitalisation or excessive interest payments may be disallowed as a deduction and recharacterized as hidden profit distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or assist in unlawful repatriation without withholding are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax; they may be served with a departure prohibition order, have their passports flagged, and face personal summary proceedings for failure to ensure statutory deduction and payment; in egregious cases, criminal prosecution for false accounting or fraud could result in imprisonment up to 2 years, and the trustee of a Chinese family trust may face civil suit for breach of fiduciary duty by beneficiaries
